result: {"thinking":"Draft has steep branches: the shell leaves the body going back up-left (way over 40 degrees) and the stalks go nearly vertical, one leaning backward. I'll give my review with concrete fixes.","review":"Body along the bottom from the tail is good, and one long spiral is the right call. Three things to change. First, the shell comes off the body heading up and back to the left, which is far too steep, so it would never fall. Have it peel off further right along the body, heading forward and up at a shallow angle, then curve up and over counterclockwise and spiral inward. Second, the stalk on the left leans backward and the other is near vertical. Let the body curve gently upward into the head, then have both stalks lean forward off it, each within about 40 degrees of the line they leave. Third, the end of the body has a kink where it bends up toward the head, so smooth that into a curve. Make the stalks a little longer too, since very short strokes break easily. Fix those and it's good to lock.","say":"Reviewed. Tom, the shell and the stalks leave the body too steeply, so they won't fall.
